Let <MATH_0001>.
Every element of <MATH_0002> is an idempotent. Hence every prime ideal is maximal
with residue field <MATH_0003>.
Thus the topology on <MATH_0004> is totally disconnected
and quasi-compact. The projection maps <MATH_0005> define open
points of <MATH_0006>. It cannot be the case that all the points
of <MATH_0007> are open since <MATH_0008> is quasi-compact. Let <MATH_0009> be a closed
point which is not open. Then we can form a scheme <MATH_0010> which is two
copies of <MATH_0011> glued along <MATH_0012>. In other words, this
is <MATH_0013> with <MATH_0014> doubled, compare
Schemes, Example <REF_0001>.
The morphism
<MATH_0015> is quasi-compact, finite type and has finite fibres
but is not quasi-separated.
The point <MATH_0016> is a generic point of an irreducible component
of <MATH_0017> (since <MATH_0018> is totally disconnected). But properties (3) and (4)
of Lemma <REF_0002> do not hold. The reason is that
for any open neighbourhood <MATH_0019> the inverse image
<MATH_0020> is not affine because functions on <MATH_0021> cannot
separate the two points lying over <MATH_0022> (proof omitted; this is a
nice exercise). Hence the condition that <MATH_0023> is quasi-separated is
necessary in parts (3) and (4) of the lemma.
